steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Engineering drawings communicate design intent precisely using standardised conventions and symbols.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Orthographic projection shows multiple 2D views: front elevation, plan and side elevation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Third angle projection places views in the orientation seen from that direction (the UK standard).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Isometric drawing shows a 3D view at 30 degrees with no perspective distortion; all axes at true scale.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain the difference between orthographic and isometric drawings. | Q: Why is a section view used in engineering drawings? | Q: Describe the information in an assembly drawing.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Orthographic shows separate 2D views (front, plan, side) for precise dimensional information. Isometric shows a single 3D view for easier visualisation but less precision for dimensioning. | A section reveals internal features (holes, chambers, wall thicknesses) hidden in external views. Hatching distinguishes solid material from empty space. | All components in assembled positions with item numbers, a parts list with descriptions, quantities and materials. Overall dimensions but usually not individual part dimensions.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the specific drawing type (orthographic, isometric, section, assembly). Third angle projection is the UK standard - state this explicitly. Section views: hatching identifies different materials and cut surfaces. Assembly drawings show HOW parts fit; detail drawings show EACH part individually. CAD/CAM: describe the full chain from 3D model to CNC output.
